fieldReports: FarFarFromHome described the reverse Tarraluoppal-Tuottar day on 2023-07-11 as easy, with the main difficulty being stream crossings requiring boots off.
Outdoorseiten's 2018 reverse-direction report described a short climb from Darreluoppal, then flatter lake terrain toward Duottar in unusually hot/dry conditions.
Komoot lists a shorter route time of about 2 hours 41 minutes, but this should not override STF/Naturkartan times for app display.

difficulty.label: short exposed high-plateau stage; not officially graded
officialClaims: STF describes rocky terrain with small lakes and snow lingering near the highest point.

Naturkartan describes easy-walked ground across dry grass heath, meadow, exposed bedrock, one usually easy ford at Gårråjávrátja, the highest point of Padjelantaleden at about 960 m, and then descent toward Darreluoppal/Tarraluoppal.
BLT/Padjelanta cabin pages identify the endpoints as remote hut sites with no road access.
keyHazards: High exposed plateau and Padjelantaleden's highest point around 950-960 m.
Late-lying snow and rapidly changing spring/early-season snow and stream conditions.
Usually easy but condition-dependent ford at or near Gårråjávrátja.
Additional small stream crossings reported in field accounts, especially in reverse direction near Darreluoppal.
Poor visibility, wind, rain, slippery wet planks/boardwalks, boggy sections, mosquitoes, and limited shelter.
Darreluoppal is just inside Sarek National Park, so boundary/rule context matters.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: No targeted follow-up batch required before writing. Import-critical facts are covered; remaining gaps are normalization decisions, exact Darreluoppal landing coordinate, bridge/ford coordinate verification, and dynamic service/currentness checks.

findings: Main thread rechecked Naturkartan BD69 GPX as 27.548 km, 1221 points, max point spacing 318.7 m, no gaps over 500 m.
Main thread confirmed BD69 starts at Darreluoppal/Tarraluoppal and ends at Stáloluokta, so section 6 must use the first stored segment reversed.
Main thread selected BD69 index 419 as the Duottar split candidate for consistency with section 5, giving a 9.753 km Darreluoppal-Duottar route-line segment.
Main thread carried the official 11 km versus computed 9.75-10.0 km discrepancy as a source contradiction rather than overriding official display distance.

importReadiness.normalizationRecommendation: Use official 11 km display distance. Use Naturkartan BD69 as the primary geometry after splitting at Duottar index 419 and reversing the Duottar-Darreluoppal segment; use OSM relation 19111626 as a cross-check and possible snap reference near Duottar. Import/deduplicate Duottar and Darreluoppal huts carefully, attach limited provisions/emergency phones/tenting as hut metadata unless standalone POIs are supported, import toilets/bridges/fords only after coordinate verification, keep the high point as a route highlight, and model Darreluoppal helicopter access as provisional boundary pickup/drop-off metadata until the landing coordinate is confirmed.
